gamespot.com/articles/2026s-best-friends.excerpt: Whether you love it or hate it, or simply wish it had a better name , friendslop is taking the world by storm. 2026 has introduced a plethora of new titles to the emerging genre, but perhaps none have had the same level of overnight success as Meccha Chameleon, a hide-and-seek style multiplayer game that puts player creativity to the test. As revealed during Nintendo's second Direct this week, Meccha Chameleon fans will soon be able purchase the game on Switch 2, though its exact launch time and price have yet to be announced. gamespot.com/articles/romancing-saga-3-i.title: Romancing SaGa 3 Is The Latest Surprise RPG Remake
gamespot.com/articles/romancing-saga-3-i.excerpt: Square Enix has announced a remake of the 1995 RPG classic, Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United , during the September Nintendo Direct. Billed as a "full 3D remake" by the company, this new version of Romancing SaGa 3 will feature upgraded graphics, fully voiced cutscenes, overhauls to combat and other mechanics, selectable difficulty levels, and several more new features. Set in a world with scheduled despair, the game follows eight protagonists on their quest to find the survivor of a calamity. Each protagonist has their own reason for doing so, but the driving force behind their actions is the Rise of Morastrum, an event that occurs every 300 years and results in all newborn life being destroyed, save for one survivor, the Child of Destiny. Like the original game, players will have the opportunity to meet and recruit over 20 other characters along the way, each with individual stats and abilities. These characters can be further fine-tuned with a Nonastrum, a star of fate that the player assigns, which influences their affinity for techs and spells. The Freeform Scenario System will also see player choices shape the characters they meet, and in battle, these warriors can "glimmer" new techniques, gain evasion skills, and perform powerful United Attacks. Square Enix added that War Mode and the Business minigame will also return, allowing players to command armies or grow a trading empire when they're not busy with the main storyline. Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United will launch for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch consoles on February 16, 2027. The SaGa series was a hit franchise for Square, with the first entry in the sci-fi RPG kicking off in 1989 on the Game Boy. A pioneer in open-world exploration and non-linear storytelling, Romancing SaGa and other entries in the franchise have periodically cropped up over the years, and in 2024, Square Enix released Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven .

gamespot.com/articles/now-you-can-play-s.title: Now You Can Play Star Fox Adventures On Switch 2 And Decide If It’s Terrible Or Great Yourself
gamespot.com/articles/now-you-can-play-s.excerpt: The black sheep of the Star Fox series, Star Fox Adventures, has landed on the Nintendo Switch Online service. As announced in the September 2026 Nintendo Direct , the GameCube title is available to play as a Nintendo Classic today for subscribers of Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack. Star Fox Adventures came out in 2002 and marked a departure from the dog-fighting gameplay the series is known for. Developed by Rare, the game began life as Dinosaur Planet for Nintendo 64 before Shigeru Miyamoto proposed converting it into a Star Fox game. Featuring Zelda-like action-adventure gameplay, Adventures has Fox McCloud stepping out of the Arwing and exploring Dinosaur Planet on foot, fighting enemies with a staff and solving environmental puzzles. Adventures also introduced the blue fox character Krystal, who later becomes the first female pilot in Star Fox. https://twitter.com/NintendoAmerica/status/2097689692883816580 Star Fox Adventures is a particularly divisive entry in the franchise, straying from the flight-combat-simulator roots of the original games and delving into Zelda-like territory. It's also famously Rare's last game for Nintendo before the studio was acquired by Microsoft. Some fans might argue that Adventures was when the franchise started to go awry, with its follow-ups Assault and Command receiving lukewarm receptions, and the eventual attempted Star Fox Zero is generally looked down on by fans and critics alike. The series did win back goodwill from fans with this year's remake of Star Fox 64 on Switch 2. Other than the shadowdrop of Star Fox Adventures, the Direct also revealed that a free update is coming to the new Star Fox game, adding new multiplayer features and maps. The Star Fox update launches on September 29.

gamespot.com/articles/ai-could-kill-all-.title: AI Could “Kill All Humans” In Next Decade, Anthropic Lead Says
gamespot.com/articles/ai-could-kill-all-.excerpt: Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger has said the AI company behind Claude and other AI products "earnestly" believes that AI "could kill all humans," and it could happen in the next decade. Posting in response to Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon's own resignation from the company due to safety concerns , Hubinger said, "We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade." He added: "I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to." Hubinger, who still works at Anthropic, went on to cite Anthropic's own latest risk report that says the risk of AI wiping out humanity from present models is "low." However, Hubinger said he is worried that superintelligence could arise from "recursive self-improvement," which is the term for AI rewriting its own code and constantly improving itself. For his part, Coxon said the AI market leaders Anthropic and OpenAI are not "acting responsibly" with regards to safety. "Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing," Coxon wrote. He said Anthropic is pushing ahead despite these concerns because the company is "locked in a race to get there first." He said a company like OpenAI isn't taking the issue seriously enough but Anthropic understands the "civilizational stakes," and, if "no one else will act responsibly ... they must do it themselves, despite the risk." Unsurprisingly, these posts have generated a lot of debate and discussion. Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont said , "AI threatens our economy, privacy, democracy and the well-being of our kids." He is lobbying Congress to "stand up to the big tech oligarchs and protect the American people."

gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-movi.excerpt: One of the talking points surrounding the upcoming Resident Evil movie is that director Zach Cregger took an original idea and slapped the Resident Evil name on it. That's not true , Cregger has said, and now he's shared more of his thought process as it relates to some of the blowback from fans of the games. He told IGN that, in retrospect, he feels it was "naive" to think that fans of the games would immediately embrace his pitch for his Resident Evil movie. "I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration," he said. "I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?" Cregger went on to say he hopes fans of the game see his movie "regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment" that he's not re-telling a story from the games. He said he hopes fans of the games "feel seen" when they watch the movie and see "all of the love for the games that are in this movie." "This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. gamespot.com/articles/blizzard-workers-w.title: Blizzard Workers Win Historic Union Contract That Could Set A New Standard For Game Developers
gamespot.com/articles/blizzard-workers-w.excerpt: A group of 1,900 employees at Blizzard Entertainment has successfully signed a union contract with Microsoft, securing several guarantees for members. Represented by the Communications Workers of America (CWA), the contract has given the Blizzard workers more workplace flexibility and guaranteed wage increases, but several other industry-first agreements could make this a blueprint for other video game unions to follow. One of the big wins for the Blizzard union is artificial intelligence guardrails, as the contract stipulates that Microsoft cannot use AI to automate or replace jobs without first talking to the union. Another big win are the job-recall rights for employees, because if they're laid off, Blizzard must offer them an open role within 14 months and inside the union's network before hiring someone from outside. Laid-off union members will also get an additional four weeks of pay--regardless of how long they worked at the company--hybrid schedules that allow them to work from home, and formal systems to settle disputes within the workplace. gamespot.com/articles/ff7-revelation-is-.excerpt: I still vividly remember the first time I played Final Fantasy VII Remake 's demo in 2019, and fully how it sold me on Square Enix's reimagining of one of the most beloved RPGs of all time. Following ex-SOLDIER Cloud's mission with Avalanche members to destroy Mako Reactor 1, the demo was perfectly paced for showcasing its beautiful modern visuals and more action-focused combat system, both of which made for an electrifying experience filled with cinematic spectacles. Fast-forward to 2026, and I'm finally playing Final Fantasy VII Revelation , the third and final part of this remake series, and it's just as surreal as it is entirely overwhelming. This is no exaggeration--when I first sat down to play the Final Fantasy VII Revelation demo at Gamescom, a Square Enix PR representative briefed us on several of the paths we could opt to take, and it became very clear that 45 minutes was not going to even be remotely close to scratching the surface of what was on offer. Basically, if you thought that Final Fantasy VII Rebirth's open world maximalism was going to be impossible to match, you haven't seen anything yet. "The idea is very much [that] we want to keep expanding, increasing the scale of the game as we go through the series," game director Naoki Hamaguchi said through a translator during a group interview. "Obviously, Remake was more of a linear story-driven game, then Rebirth turned into an explorable open world. Taking Rebirth to Revelation, we wanted to expand that with the feeling of verticality. The world's not just going outwards, it's also going upwards as well." That sentiment was very evident in the demo, which started at Chapter 4 of the game on the Highwind, an airship that you can fly all across the world.
